title: Wrong role listed for animal_type
description: Prior to my change, if you run the "role-sum" cell's solution, it lists `animal_type`'s role as `outcome`. I think this is a namespace issue where it is using pca_rec as defined at line 50 rather than as defined in "role" cell. Unless there is way to update the global namespace version of the pca_rec object, it looks like you need to add these lines of code to make animal_name and animal_type both come out with role listed as `id`.

title: Fix `plot_top_loadings()`
description:
Closes #14 

After looking at this in detail, I'm not sure if this function ever worked, actually.

Here are the new results:

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'tune':
#>   method                   from   
#>   required_pkgs.model_spec parsnip
library(learntidymodels)
#> Loading required package: tidyverse
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal())


data("cells", package = "modeldata")
cell_pca <-
    recipe(class ~ ., data = cells %>% dplyr::select(-case)) %>%
    step_center(all_predictors()) %>%
    step_scale(all_predictors()) %>%
    step_pca(all_predictors())

cell_pca <- prep(cell_pca)

plot_top_loadings(cell_pca, grepl("ch_1", terms) & component_number <= 4, n = 10)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/JIBtpEo.png)

title: Updates to pca-recipes tutorial and package handling
description:
This PR includes,

1. Updated `DESCRIPTION`: `tidymodels` and `tidyverse` are moved to depends, all individual core packages of the meta packages removed from import.
1. With this PR tutorials are no longer included in `.Rbuildignore`, will update this once we have a solution. 
1. Tutorial name change to `pca-recipes` (it was `pca_recipe`).
1. Updates to`pca-recipes` tutorial: now now attaches meta-packages in the tutorial (e.g. `library(tidymodels`), shaves the correlation plot diagonally, includes a final section with resources, other necessary fixes for plotting steps, typos, and additional explanations.

Adding tidymodels CSS from Desiree
description: This PR adds an example learnr tutorial using `usethis::use_tutorial()` and adding the tidymodels.org learnr CSS style from @dcossyleon. Note: for now, I think this CSS file will need to be placed inside each tutorial's folder. A more scalable method, since this is already a package, is to wrap the learnr output format in our own custom format, see: https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/format-derive.html
